KELLEY OF MICHIGAN D ‘Former Congressman, Ex / pert on Naval Affairs, Passes Away at Washing ton Washington, Sept. 11—(A.P.) Former Representative Patrick H. Kelley of Michigan died here early today after a prolonged illness. A Republican leader of the House from the 6th Michigan district for five terms, 1921-23, Mr Kelley, who was 58, was most prominently identified with naval matters, serving as chairman of the naval subcommittee of the House appropriations committee. In this capacity he helped frame several naval i bills. During his last term he engaged |in a long but unsuccessful fight against j the provision in the 1923 naval bill te increase the navy's enlisted strength from 67,000 to 86,000, which had the ;indorsement of President Harding. . Born in Cass county, Michigan, October 7, 1867, he graduated from the University of Michigan in 1900 and began the practice of law at Lansing the same year. He was a member of the Michigan state board of education, state superintendent of public instruction and lieutenant-governor of the state from 1907-11.
